tool_input.message:
Round-2 result for m-2026-10-22-048 is submitted through ethos (verdict pass, confidence 0.85).

I made three round-2 commits on design/opencode-plugin-adapter, touching only `docs/spec-opencode-lifecycle.tex`: 7d29298, 1bee4b2 and e905e0c. fuzz and `make check` were clean before each. Nothing is pushed.

**C12, ruled option (c):**
- `assumeNoTierBOverFork` is gone. The new switch `fixDurableName` keeps the pending record for the life of the claim as the durable name of the fork skeleton.
- `LcCfFinish` now keeps the record and marks it complete in a new field, `pendDone`. The record is removed only by `mission release`, by the close-time claim clearing, or by `deleteFiles`. Each first closes the skeleton the record names (fork kind, owned by the session, compare-and-set on verdict open).
- With the switch off, `NoOrphanOpenSkeleton` fails (`C12_off`, 60,514 states, depth 11): complete a propagation, then a Tier B dispatch over the fork binding.
- With it on and no assumption, it holds over all 257,269 states of the claim+ slice, which includes Tier B over fork, operator claim, mission close and clearing.
- A complete record is never resumable, since `LcCfReconcileReuse` now requires the child not be in `pendDone`.
- "Live" now means the child's claim is for the skeleton's mission, whatever the binding names, for a complete record. An incomplete record is live only if the binding also names it, as in C4. A live record is kept and marked complete.
- The `leaked` and `liveAborted` ghosts use the same notion of live.
- Re-checked with the switch on, all holding: `ReconcileOnExit`, `SweepComplete`, `LiveSpared`, `LockedWrites`, `NoForeignAbort`, and `WellFormed` (now including `pendDone`).
- Mutants killed: the record removed at finish (`MutFinishRec`, `NoOrphanOpenSkeleton` counterexample) and a complete record judged live by the binding alone (`MutLiveNoDone`, `LiveSpared` counterexample). The round-1 mutants were re-run and all die. `MutA_claimed` had silently stopped mutating after the edit; I re-pointed it at the new text and it dies again.

**Reuse supersede clause, ruled keep as defensive:** the ledger and verification now say it is unexercised, not verified. `Reach_all` visited all 257,269 states and found none with a record, no claim and another open fork binding. `Reach_nosup` (supersede off, record not durable) reaches that state; `Reach_nosup_dur` does not.

**Two other results to know about:**
- `MutReuseDone` (a complete record treated as resumable) survives. Every operation that takes the claim away closes the skeleton and removes the record, so the guard is defensive. Your instruction was to model the complete/crashed distinction and check it; it is checked in the claimed case by `MutLiveNoDone`, not by this guard.
- With the durable record, `fixReleaseCloses` and `fixSupersede` are no longer needed for `NoOrphanOpenSkeleton`. `Fa_orph_norel_dur` and `C9_nosup_dur` hold, while the same rows with the switch off are counterexamples. I kept both switches and recorded this in the ledger; whether the code keeps them is your call.

**Verification:** I re-ran all 96 rows on the round-2 model.
- The bounded full-machine rows (200,000, 40,000 and 200,000 states) found no counterexample but are not exhaustive.
- The `/z-spec:test` run at setsize 1 gives the same figures as before: 6,496 states, 213,008 transitions, 5 of 6 checks. Coverage fails by design because 17 operations need two sessions.

**Design sections that must change, beyond the round-1 list:**
- The §5 point 2 item 5 sentences "removed as the last step of a successful write" and "the record is then overwritten or removed".
- The record format needs a stage field (complete or not).
- `ClearMissionBindings` (`internal/mission/active.go`:907-957) must also close and remove the record-named skeleton when it clears a claim. That is a change to an existing Claude Code path.
- `mission release` and `deleteFiles` close the record-named skeleton before removing the record.
- The "record does not parse" row of the exit-status table now applies for as long as the claim lasts.
- The Tier B dispatch path is unchanged.

Files are in <repo>:
- docs/spec-opencode-lifecycle.tex
- .tmp/lc3/rows4.txt (the 96 rows)
- .tmp/lc3/r6/ (probcli outputs)
- .tmp/lc3/result2.yaml

tool_input.message:
VERDICT: ACCEPT m-2026-10-22-048 round 2, conditional on one mechanical correction (B1: two wrong table cells) that needs no re-verification. Everything else I tried reproduces. I changed nothing in the repository; my scratch files are in .tmp/jra3/ (exp3.sh, cmp.py, my*.py mutants, r6/ outputs).

## 1. Reproduction (my own runs on commit e905e0c, using the worker's x2.sh slicer and goals; counts equal the table)

| Row | Outcome | States |
|---|---|---|
| C12_off (NoOrphan, claim+ slice) | counterexample | 60514 |
| C12_on / C9_all (NoOrphan, claim+ slice) | holds, all visited | 257269 |
| F1D_off / F1P_off / F1R_off (NoForeignAbort) | counterexample | 84 / 337 / 191 |
| F1D_on / F1P_on / F1R_on | holds, all visited | 11073 / 33217 / 2013 |
| S_lin_off (LineageStable with SessionStart) | counterexample | 44 |
| S_lin_on and S_acyc_on | hold, all visited | 1025 each |
| Fv_off / Fv2_off (NoVerdictOverwrite) | counterexample | 1198 / 5838 |
| Fv_on | holds, all visited | 19697 |
| Fv2_on | bounded, no counterexample | 300000 |
| Fa_lockw_off (LockedWrites) | counterexample | 1857 |
| Fa_lockw_all | holds, all visited | 16601 |
| Fa_live_all (LiveSpared) | holds, all visited | 16601 |
| Fa_orph_all | holds, all visited | 16601 |

- The 257,269-state NoOrphanOpenSkeleton row is reproduced.
- I checked every row in the lifecycle spec against the worker's raw outputs in .tmp/lc3/r6: 96 rows, 2 mismatches (see B1).
- fixes off versus on behave as claimed for C12, F1, F3, F10 and F9.

## 2. My own mutants of the durable record (claim+ slice, all fifteen switches on, 2/2/2)

| Mutant | Goal | Result |
|---|---|---|
| MyFinishRm (Finish removes the record, the old behaviour) | NoOrphan | killed, 60514 states (C12 returns) |
| MyRelNoClose (release removes the record but closes nothing) | NoOrphan | killed, 48840 states |
| MyReuseComplete (a complete record treated as resumable; guard `c ∉ pendDone` dropped) | NoOrphan and LiveSpared | survives, 257269 states, all visited |
| MyRelKeepRec (release closes but leaves the record) | NoOrphan and LiveSpared | survives, 318189 states |
| MyRefuseDropRec | – | invalid: I conjoined an unsatisfiable term, so the transition was merely disabled; discard |

- **MyReuseComplete** survives for the reason the worker states. The combination "complete record, no claim, open skeleton, open mission" is unreachable, because every claim-removing path also closes and unnames. The `pendDone` guard in LcCfReconcileReuse is therefore defensive and unverified, as lifecycle.tex:2480-2488 says.
- **MyRelKeepRec** shows that "release also removes the record" is unchecked. Keeping the record is harmless in the model, because a closed skeleton is not resumable. Record clearance on release is hygiene, not an invariant, and the text should not describe it as verified (non-blocking, N3 below).

## 3. Fidelity

- **LcTierBDispatch** (pretooluse_dispatch.go:880-884).
  - It matches: the binding is written with ParentSession equal to the session itself, naming the new skeleton and overwriting the previous one. The skeleton stays open, and CloseDelegationSkeleton has no verdict test (delegation.go:675-683, so the CAS is a code change). The consequences list names delegation.go:649-692.
  - Omitted paths: the model requires `s? ∈ roster`, which the code does not. It omits the depth-gate close with verdict `aborted` (a Tier B skeleton closed in dispatch, not by deleteFiles or reconcile) and the non-fatal binding-write failure. None of these affects NoForeignAbort.
- **LcSessionStart** (session_start.go:69,194).
  - It matches. The code reads no source and always calls CreateInCheckout, which rewrites the roster. The unfixed non-fork branch models exactly that (corrupt cleared, sealed emptied). The fixed branch is the Ensure create-if-absent path.
- **Release** (cmd/ethos/mission.go:2135-2179).
  - The code clears the claim and binding without any lock, and takes the dispatch-pending lock only for ClearDispatchPending. It is idempotent with no claim.
  - The model's LcReleaseClaim is atomic, requires `s? ∉ dom stage`, and requires `s? ∈ dom claimed`. So the race between release and an in-flight claim-forked write phase is excluded by assumption, and the no-claim idempotent release (record and binding present, claim absent) is not represented.
- **Close-time clearing** (mission/active.go:907-957).
  - LcClearClosed matches. The claim and the binding are cleared by two independent tests, as in the code. The same unlocked-clear caveat applies.
- **Close-time closing of the fork skeleton.**
  - That the clearing also closes the record-named skeleton is correctly flagged as a code change in the consequences. It is redundant in the model, since the sweep has already closed it, so it is unverified.

## 4. Invariant conventions and ghosts

- Every invariant is a `LcInv…` schema (docs/spec-opencode-lifecycle.tex:428-486) and is run as a negated `-goal` (goals.sh). The state schema Lifecycle (:335) has no predicate part.
- The ghosts (`leaked`, `overwritten`, `liveAborted`, `unlocked`) are computed from the post-state by one rule per ghost. I confirmed this at :1008, 1043, 1108, 1161-1164, 1232-1236 and 1583. The earlier vacuity defect is not present.
- The literal NoOrphanOpenSkeleton (:449) is weakened by the durable record, since the record now names a skeleton for the life of the claim. The strength comes from the mutants above, which die, plus ReconcileOnExit and LiveSpared.

## 5. Findings

**B1. Blocking, mechanical.** Two table cells contradict the worker's own raw outputs and the prose.
- docs/spec-opencode-lifecycle.tex:2452 `MutA_claimed`: the table says "holds, all states visited, 50 321 states, depth 27". The worker's output (.tmp/lc3/r6/MutA_claimed.out) and my re-run give a counterexample at 2818 states, depth 12. The trace is C4 (WriteBinding, Crash, OperatorClaim, Begin, ReconcileClaimed), as the prose at :2420-2424 says. The mutant dies; the table must say so.
- :2409 `Reach_nosup`: the table says "holds, 257 269". The raw output is a counterexample at 218544 states, and the prose at :2490-2494 says it is reachable at depth 17. The cell is wrong.
- :2493 cites `Reach_nosup_dur`, which has no table row. Its output is "holds, all visited, 257269". Add the row.
- After these corrections the table, prose and raw outputs agree.

**N1. Non-blocking.** State in the limits the release and close-time clearing assumptions: the code clears the claim and binding unlocked and idempotently without a claim (mission.go:2135-2179), whereas the model is atomic, locked and requires a claim. The implementation of `mission release` must take the child's dispatch-pending lock around the whole sequence (close, unname, clear), or the C11/C12 closes can race a write phase.

**N2. Non-blocking.** Add the Tier B omissions of section 3 (no-roster dispatch, depth-gate close, failed binding write) to the limits.

**N3. Non-blocking.** MyReuseComplete and MyRelKeepRec survive. The text already admits the first. Add that "release removes the record" is likewise unverified, so no reader treats it as checked.

**N4. Non-blocking, carried over.** The F2/F3/Chain rows and Fv2_on remain bounded (40000-300000 states) and are marked as such. I found nothing in them that contradicts the results.

No further modelling round is needed. Once the leader corrects the cells in B1, I would accept without a re-run.
